PullRequest.Title: chat: hide ineligible plugin skills from slash completions

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/348234

Plugin skills marked `user-invocable: false` could reappear in slash autocomplete when the SDK listed them: the runtime completion provider treated known but ineligible skills as unknown. Keep these skills, disabled children, and skills in disabled containers out of runtime suggestions using their exact command names and aliases.

## Before / After

Completion-provider tests with an SDK runtime catalog:

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/my-plugin:user-disabled`, with `disableUserInvocation: true` | Offered | Hidden |
| Hidden synced skill whose bare name is reserved, such as `/skills-bundle:plan` | Offered | Hidden |
| Eligible synced skill with that reserved name | Offered by qualified name | Unchanged |
| Unrelated bare `/hidden` alongside hidden `my-plugin:hidden` | Offered | Unchanged |

Visible-skill deduplication, real-plugin namespacing, unknown runtime skills, and non-skill commands remain intact. This changes autocomplete only, not model invocation or SDK/protocol contracts.

## Validation

Using Node 24.22.1:

- `pnpm run build-fast --client-only` — passed; refreshed compiled output.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotSlashCommandCompletionProvider.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostSkillCompletionProvider.test.ts --reporter dot` — passed, 116 tests.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `pnpm run oxlint src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotSlashCommandCompletionProvider.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotSlashCommandCompletionProvider.test.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed. Commit hygiene hooks also passed.
- Before the production fix, `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotSlashCommandCompletionProvider.test.ts --grep 'runtime skill completions' --reporter dot` — 18 passed and four regressions failed as expected.

No live editor/Agents window reproduction or real-provider model-invocation test was performed. The original editor observation's backend remains unidentified.

_🤖 Posted by GitHub Copilot on Harald's behalf._

Scenarios.Scenario: Copilot CLI slash-command and inline skill autocomplete while typing
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each completion request waits for the runtime command catalog and the session customization snapshot in parallel, then synchronously scans runtime commands before returning suggestions. The diff adds construction of an ineligible-skill set and set lookups/lowercasing during that scan, all on the completion critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List SDK runtime slash commands on a cold runtime-catalog lookup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one coalesced commands.list RPC per cache generation; subsequent completion requests use the cached catalog until invalidation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same runtime command lookup was already executed for every runtime-completion path before this diff, with the same cache and coalescing behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold completion waits up to the configured completion timeout; warm completion reads the cached catalog.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Settle customization discovery/parsing and refresh the published customization snapshot, including plugin and MCP discovery work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One session-customization request per relevant completion invocation; underlying discovered entries and synchronization promises are shared/cached by the session plugin controller, while pending refreshes are awaited together.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: _getKnownSkills already fetched and enumerated the same session customizations on this path; the diff does not add or increase boundary calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Completion waits for the customization snapshot before filtering known and ineligible skills.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Transport the completion request/result between the workbench and Agent Host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One completion request per editor suggestion invocation, commonly repeated as the user types.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The autocomplete transport and invocation frequency are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The provider result must return before suggestions are shown.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: CPU/allocation grows linearly with the number of configured skill customizations, plus alias checks across runtime skill commands. Realistic effective cardinality is the session's deduplicated runtime command catalog and current customization snapshot, not files or workspace items. The diff adds at most one candidate string per ineligible skill, plus one qualified plugin identity, and constant-time set membership per runtime skill/alias.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The runtime-command lookup and customization lookup run concurrently via Promise.all. Completion providers also run concurrently via Promise.allSettled. Runtime catalog misses are coalesced by one in-flight promise; the changed in-memory filtering itself is single-threaded and has no new burst or limiter requirement.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The runtime command catalog has positive caching and in-flight coalescing; on timeout it can return an existing cached value or an empty catalog while the shared refresh continues. Session customization state is owned by long-lived discovery/controller objects and the completion path awaits their settled snapshot. The new ineligible set is rebuilt per completion and not retained, but its size is bounded by the current customization snapshot and adds only linear in-memory work alongside the pre-existing full enumeration.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the changed O(skills + runtime aliases) transient CPU/allocation mechanism and in its autocomplete critical-path placement; high confidence that it is incremental to an already linear scan and does not constitute a concrete actionable regression at evidenced scales.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large plugin/skill catalogs would increase transient string/set allocation on each keystroke, but repository evidence does not establish realistic cardinalities large enough for this incremental work to cause noticeable latency or GC pressure. No new boundary call, cache miss, or concurrency amplification is introduced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The added set construction and lookups are necessary bounded in-memory filtering over data already fetched and traversed; they neither add expensive boundaries nor materially amplify frequency, cardinality, retention, or concurrency.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete two-file diff and traced the autocomplete path through runtime-command caching, session customization discovery, provider concurrency, and per-command filtering. The production change adds bounded transient set/string work per completion but no new IPC/filesystem/network operation, cache lifecycle change, retained state, or realistic high-impact scaling mechanism. Test-only changes introduce no product-path performance behavior.
